message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"2.53","text":"Nevertheless, at the proper time I will also give you an explanation of these matters together with similar ones. But for now, as you see, since evening has overtaken us, let the things said today be sufficient. On another occasion, if you wish, feel free to ask us about whatever you want, and we will gladly explain them without hesitation. After saying this, he got up. And so, after partaking of food, we turned to sleep, for night had overtaken us.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τὴν ἐπίλυσιν","chosen":"an explanation","rationale":"The noun can denote an explanation or solution; the context concerns resolving the hearer's questions."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ δὲ λοιποῦ","chosen":"But for now","rationale":"The phrase can mean “for the rest,” “for the remaining time,” or “henceforth.” The evening context supports taking it as a transition that closes the present session."},{"source_quote":"θαρρῶν ἡμῖν πυνθάνου","chosen":"feel free to ask us","rationale":"This expresses the participle’s call for confidence in idiomatic modern English while retaining the invitation to inquire."},{"source_quote":"χαίροντες ἀόκνως ἐπιλύσομεν","chosen":"we will gladly explain them without hesitation","rationale":"The participle χαίροντες conveys gladness, ἀόκνως readiness or lack of hesitation, and ἐπιλύσομεν the explaining or resolving of the matters raised."},{"source_quote":"ἐγήγερται","chosen":"he got up","rationale":"The perfect is used in the narrative sequence for the completed action of rising."},{"source_quote":"εἰς ὕπνον ἐτράπημεν","chosen":"we turned to sleep","rationale":"This retains the source’s image of turning toward sleep rather than replacing it with the less transparent “went to bed.”"},{"source_quote":"κατειλήφει γὰρ ἡ νύξ","chosen":"for night had overtaken us","rationale":"The rendering preserves both the pluperfect force and the image of night catching or overtaking the group; “us” is implicit from the context."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"καὶ οὕτως. τροφῆς μεταλαβόντες","issue":"The printed full stop leaves καὶ οὕτως as an elliptical sentence or separates an adverb naturally attachable to the following participial clause. The translation adopts the latter attachment; alternatively the print may be represented as “And so it was. After partaking of food ...” This is an editorial punctuation ambiguity, not unreadable or missing text.","proposed_reading":"καὶ οὕτως, τροφῆς μεταλαβόντες","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
